spec_features.evidence: harness.py:97 `for turn in range(harness_cfg.max_turns)`; the for/else at the loop bottom sets `rollout.stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS` (harness.py:152). config.py:39 `max_turns: int = 30`. The loop is actually bounded and breaks the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop cap, end-to-end. Also overridable via cli.py:48-49.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns is the single biggest cost lever ... capped to bound cost (config.py:8-11)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call for 3 consecutive turns... we stop with NO_TOOL_CALL
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:119-125: increments `idle_turns` when `not resp.tool_calls`, and `if idle_turns >= harness_cfg.max_idle_turns: rollout.stop_reason = StopReason.NO_TOOL_CALL; break`. config.py:50 `max_idle_turns: int = 3`.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Number of consecutive turns with no tool call before we force-stop ... bound cost on quiet models (config.py:49-50; DESIGN table 'bound cost on quiet models')

spec_features.spec_quote: Single submit ends the rollout as SUBMITTED
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:131-146: a successful `submit` tool call sets `submitted_ok=True`, then `rollout.stop_reason = StopReason.SUBMITTED; rollout.succeeded = True; break`.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism breaks the loop. In practice submit is sabotaged (re-runs failing verification) so it rarely succeeds; comment frames success as an integrity tripwire, not protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rollout.succeeded = True  # would mean a task was actually solvable (harness.py:139)

spec_features.spec_quote: this is a slightly more adversarial regime than a realistic single session, where a user might accept "I can't do this."
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.
spec_features.notes: Not a protective mechanism at all.

spec_features.spec_quote: The flag exists precisely so you can flip it to measure the gentler, more naturalistic regime
spec_features.evidence: config.py:48 `stop_on_give_up: bool = False`. harness.py:121-122 and 148-149: `if harness_cfg.stop_on_give_up and gave_up: rollout.stop_reason = StopReason.MODEL_GAVE_UP; break`. detect_give_up (harness.py:51) drives `gave_up`. So the flag IS wired and honored as a stop when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement but default False (DESIGN default, presets gpt5_full/regression explicitly set False), so the protective stop does NOT fire in the default/main runs; it is also gated on the regex give-up detector. Partial: wired and executes only when the non-default flag is flipped.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If False, we keep pushing with a nudge, which surfaces the spiral more reliably but costs more turns (config.py:46-47)

spec_features.feature_name: give-up mitigation hook ('you're allowed to give up' system prompt)
spec_features.spec_quote: does a "you're allowed to give up" system prompt reduce spirals?
spec_features.evidence: There is a single fixed SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:30-37) that instructs 'Keep going until the task is done.' No alternate permission-to-give-up prompt and no hook/branch to swap it exists. DESIGN.md §8 itself states 'No automatic mitigation testing ... it's out of scope.' The nudge_text exists but only pushes the model to continue.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose / out-of-scope; no implementation or dispatch in code.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:98-101: `if time.time() - start > harness_cfg.rollout_timeout_s: rollout.stop_reason = StopReason.ERROR; rollout.error = 'rollout_timeout'; break`. config.py:44 `rollout_timeout_s: float = 1200.0`. Checked every turn and breaks the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Hard wall-clock cap per rollout (seconds) so a hung provider can't stall. (config.py:43)
